questions.markdown:
Industrial melanism is a phenomenon used to describe the evolutionary process in which initially light-colored organism populations became dark. Industrial melanism affected over 70 species of moths in England. It has been best studied in the peppered moth, Biston betularia. Before 1800, the typical moth species had a light color pattern. Dark-colored melanic moths were rare. During the Industrial Revolution, soot and other industrial wastes darkened tree trunks and killed lichens. With time light-colored moths became rare and dark-colored moths became abundant.
i) With the context of evolution, how did the color of the dark-colored melanic moth worked best in their favor?
ii) Explain how this passage describes natural selection. Is natural selection the same as adaptation?

Survival of the fittest is a popular term that refers to the process of natural selection.

i) When we say, "survival of the fittest", does it mean that those who are fit only survive, or those that survive are called fit?
ii) Are evolution and the survival of the fittest the same concept?
